threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You start referring to the bus stops by their old names instead of the new ones. Locals will spot that misstep right away.
Last night on the 37, a lady brought her pet ferret on board. It was just chilling in her backpack, poking its head out. Classic Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy selling fresh baklava by the U-Bahn while a busker played Turkish folk tunes. That mix is Neukölln in a nutshell.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg does your late-night döner come with a side of karaoke from the kebab shop next door. It's wild and somehow comforting.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they curse at BART delays while still finishing their burrito from La Taqueria.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 in rush hour, packed like sardines. An accordion player jumped on and played ‘La Vie en Rose’. It was surreal amid the chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars in Gràcia are trendy, but some of the best ones are hidden in back alleys, where old locals still sit playing cards.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still take photos of every menu and can't resist asking for a 'mojito de fresa' at a traditional tapas bar.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look around for a bus stop sign instead of a handwritten 'bus stop' chalkboard outside the pub. That's a sure newbie giveaway.
Caught a lad on the 3 bus singing an opera aria at 2 AM, completely off-key but so passionate that half the bus joined in. Classic Brixton moment!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard the unmistakable sound of a saxophonist jamming from a rooftop during the weekend flea market. That’s Neukölln in a nutshell.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings, complete with a makeshift bar and a DJ in the corner. It's pure magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they know that the N-Judah is just as unreliable as the weather here—both can ruin your day without warning.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, I saw a dog on a leash riding the 16th Street bus, calmly watching the streetcars. Only in SF do you see pooches treating transit like a joyride.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the quiet corners where locals sip coffee and debate politics like it’s a sport.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're recent when they still think it's a good idea to walk around with a map, even though Google Maps is everywhere.
